questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Chain of Responsibility pattern?

options.text: Pass a request along a chain of handlers until one handles it, decoupling sender from receiver
Encapsulate a request as an object
Ensure a class has a single instance
Share intrinsic state across many objects

questions.explanation: CoR chains handlers and forwards the request. Encapsulating a request as an object = Command; one instance = Singleton; sharing state = Flyweight.

questions.prompt: When a handler receives a request, what are its two options?

options.text: Handle it, or forward it to the next handler
Clone it, or delete it
Encrypt it, or cache it
Convert it, or simplify it

questions.explanation: Each handler either processes the request or passes it along the chain.

questions.prompt: Why might a request go unhandled in this pattern?

options.text: No handler is guaranteed to act, so a request can reach the end of the chain without being processed
Requests are always handled by the first handler
The chain deep-copies every request
Handlers can only run once per program

questions.explanation: The pattern doesn't guarantee handling; you must add a default/terminal handler if handling is required.

questions.prompt: Why does the order of handlers matter?

options.text: The request travels through handlers in sequence, so reordering changes the outcome
Order never matters in this pattern
Only the last handler ever runs
Handlers run in random order

questions.explanation: Because handlers see the request in order, putting auth before or after validation produces different behavior.

questions.prompt: Which everyday web construct is an example of Chain of Responsibility?

options.text: Middleware, where each layer either responds or calls next()
A database index
A CSS stylesheet
A DNS record

questions.explanation: Middleware chains handlers that each inspect the request and either handle it or forward it.

questions.prompt: Which are genuine benefits of Chain of Responsibility? Select all that apply.

options.text: The sender is decoupled from whichever receiver acts
Handlers can be added, removed, or reordered
Every request is guaranteed to be handled
Each handler can stay small and single-purpose

questions.explanation: CoR decouples sender and receiver, supports flexible chains, and keeps handlers focused. It does NOT guarantee a request is handled.
